title: SSE-S3 vs SSE-KMS vs client-side encryption
hint: SSE-S3: AWS owns/manages keys, no audit trail of key use. SSE-KMS: you control the key (policy, rotation, CloudTrail logging of usage). Client-side: data encrypted before upload; even AWS/DBAs can't read it.

title: SQS vs SNS vs Kinesis vs EventBridge
hint: SQS = queue/buffer, one consumer per message, decoupling, DLQ. SNS = pub/sub fan-out push. Kinesis = ordered, replayable real-time stream, many consumers. EventBridge = event bus with rules, schedules, SaaS/AWS service events. FIFO (SQS/SNS) when order matters.

title: Multi-AZ vs Read Replica vs Aurora Global
hint: Multi-AZ = synchronous standby for HA/failover, not readable (instance deployment). Read replica = async copy to offload reads/reports, can be cross-Region. Aurora Global Database = cross-Region DR with <1s replication lag.

title: Gateway vs Interface VPC endpoint
hint: Gateway endpoint: only S3 and DynamoDB, free, added as a route-table target, not reachable from on-prem. Interface endpoint (PrivateLink): ENI with private IP in your subnet, most services, costs per hour/GB, reachable via VPN/Direct Connect.

title: NAT Gateway vs NAT instance vs Egress-only IGW
hint: NAT gateway: managed, scales, AZ-scoped (one per AZ for HA), lives in a public subnet. NAT instance: self-managed EC2, legacy. Egress-only internet gateway: the IPv6 equivalent (outbound only).

title: EFS vs FSx (Windows / Lustre / ONTAP) vs EBS
hint: EFS: Linux NFS, shared across AZs, POSIX. FSx for Windows: SMB + Active Directory. FSx for Lustre: HPC, sub-ms, S3-linked. FSx for ONTAP: NFS + SMB multi-protocol, SnapMirror. EBS: block storage for one instance (io2 Multi-Attach is the exception, same AZ).

title: Storage Gateway types
hint: S3 File Gateway: NFS/SMB → S3 objects (lifecycle-able). FSx File Gateway: low-latency cache for FSx Windows. Volume Gateway cached: data in S3, hot data local. Volume Gateway stored: full data local, async backup to S3. Tape Gateway: iSCSI VTL replacing physical tapes.

title: Spot vs Reserved vs Savings Plans vs On-Demand
hint: Spot: up to 90% off, can be interrupted (stateless/batch/fault-tolerant). Reserved Instances: steady 24/7 baseline, specific family. Compute Savings Plan: commitment in $/h, flexible across family/Region/Fargate/Lambda. On-Demand: short, unpredictable, no interruption.

title: DataSync vs Snow Family vs Transfer Family vs Storage Gateway
hint: DataSync: online, scheduled/one-time bulk copy with bandwidth throttling + integrity checks. Snow Family: offline when bandwidth/time is too small (do the math: TB / Mbps). Transfer Family: SFTP/FTPS/AS2 endpoint into S3/EFS. Storage Gateway: ongoing hybrid access.

title: CloudFront vs Global Accelerator
hint: CloudFront: HTTP(S) caching CDN, signed URLs, geo restriction, Lambda@Edge. Global Accelerator: TCP/UDP, 2 static anycast IPs, fast regional failover, no caching.

title: Object Lock governance vs compliance vs legal hold vs Vault Lock
hint: Compliance mode: nobody (not even root) can delete before retention ends. Governance: users with special permission can override. Legal hold: no expiry, removed with s3:PutObjectLegalHold. AWS Backup Vault Lock: WORM for backups.

title: CloudTrail vs Config vs CloudWatch
hint: CloudTrail: who called which API (audit). Config: resource configuration history + compliance rules. CloudWatch: metrics, logs, alarms, dashboards.

title: Secrets Manager vs Parameter Store
hint: Secrets Manager: built-in automatic rotation (RDS/Aurora), cross-Region replication, costs per secret. Parameter Store SecureString: cheap/free config + secrets, no native rotation.
